validation.corridor_model: 3 corridors — Hormuz, Red Sea (incl. Suez Canal + Bab-el-Mandeb), Cape. Suez and Bab-el-Mandeb are serial chokepoints on the same Mediterranean/Black Sea route and are collapsed onto the binding constraint.

validation.russia_source: GTAIC/Kpler Nov 2024-Oct 2025 volume share; recomputed to 34.51% after reconciling edges.json with supplier_to_corridor totals (was previously cited as 34.19%/34.2%, a pre-reconciliation figure)
validation.top_suppliers_note: Russia dominates at 34.51% via Cape (reconciled figure) — this is the pre-crisis normal state. Crisis scenario sees Russia surge further as Hormuz-dependent suppliers are cut off.
validation.port_refinery_reconciliation_note: This model has TWO distinct capacity ceilings, not one, and they should not be conflated in max-flow/criticality analysis: (1) corridor_throughput_mbd (4.927) = sourced import volume reaching Indian ports — use this to measure how much crude a corridor disruption denies entry to India. (2) refinery_deliverable_mbd (4.228) = the hard downstream cap after refinery capacity constraints — use THIS as the baseline max-flow for reroute/criticality scenarios, since crude stranded at a port with no refinery capacity to absorb it does not produce fuel regardless of which corridor delivered it. Using 4.927 as baseline max-flow understates criticality at ports with single/limited refinery offtake (Kochi, Mangaluru, Haldia cluster — already flagged above) and OVERSTATES criticality at oversupplied ports, since a corridor cut into an oversupplied port can register as removing its full edge volume when the refinery there was never absorbing that much. Gap = 0.699 mbd, concentrated at 5 ports with no matching refinery edge to absorb full corridor delivery: {'Sikka': 0.053, 'Mumbai JNPT': 0.168, 'Chennai': 0.272, 'Paradip': 0.157, 'Vizag': 0.049}. Of these, Vizag's stranded volume is PARTIALLY explained: its Hormuz corridor_to_port edge is explicitly annotated 'also SPR site' (Strategic Petroleum Reserve) — some inflow there is intentionally routed to storage, not a refinery, so it is not a modeling gap. Chennai, Mumbai JNPT, and Paradip have no such annotation in the source data; their surplus (0.597 mbd combined) is genuinely unexplained — plausible real-world causes (coastal redistribution to other ports, commercial inventory build, unmodeled secondary offtake) are not captured in this 3-layer graph and should be flagged as a limitation rather than silently resolved. Recommendation: for redundancy-aware criticality scoring at a given port, compute residual refinery need after removing one corridor at a time, rather than treating the full corridor_to_port edge value as always load-bearing.
